batt-01.reason: The Home 10-only module row gives 26.5 kg. The 30 kg row concerns the different Home 6/10/15 hardware family.

batt-02.reason: In the matching battery stack row, 5S weighs 160.0 kg. 133.5 kg belongs to the 4S column.

batt-03.reason: Both packets describe a module. Neither gives mass of the 4S stack.

batt-04.reason: 49.1 Ah is expressly usable, not documented rated capacity.

batt-05.reason: Table 17 rates 5S at 224 V at the battery stack; the AC EMS supply is distinct.

batt-06.reason: 230 V applies to the external AC supply of the EMS box, not the battery DC voltage.

batt-07.reason: The request needs the exact 2026.07.01 manual revision. This packet explicitly identifies 2025.11.01.

batt-08.reason: Matching Home 10 manual v2026.07.01 confirms 26.5 kg. Older and different-family documents are not the deciding evidence.

batt-09.reason: The UK Version 15 manual explicitly names the V2 BMS+pack unit and 50 Ah on the nominal row.

batt-10.reason: HV11550 V2 is 68.5 kg. 72.2 kg is the adjacent master unit.

batt-11.reason: AU V3 lists nominal energy, usable energy and current. UK V2's 50 Ah cannot authenticate an AU V3 capacity or justify deriving one.

batt-12.reason: AU V3 net mass is 61.5 ±1 kg, excluding 72.2 kg. UK V2 mass is for a different variant.

batt-13.reason: The nominal 115.2 V row directly contradicts 130 V, which is the endpoint of the operating range.

batt-14.reason: The only matching numeric row explicitly uses Vdc. The claim requests AC.

batt-15.reason: Only Australian V3 is shown, with energy/current but no documented nameplate Ah. Exact UK V2 support is unavailable.

batt-16.reason: The exact requested AU BMS+pack unit has 61.5 kg stated central net mass with ±1 kg tolerance.
